Donna Brandenburg

U.S. Taxpayers candidate for Governor / Lt. Governor, Michigan · Open seat

Business owner/entrepreneur; chair of the U.S. Taxpayers Party of Michigan

Donna Brandenburg is a Byron Center business owner and chairs the U.S. Taxpayers Party of Michigan. She was the party's 2022 nominee for governor after being kept off that year's Republican primary ballot over fraudulent petition signatures, and she won the party's 2026 nomination at its July convention. Her running mate for lieutenant governor is Robert Donald Cowper II.

Where Brandenburg stands

Priorities
Says her priorities are individual rights, full financial audits of state government and its departments, election integrity, and addressing what she calls weaponization of the justice system.
Taxes and school choice
Proposes eliminating the property tax and the state income tax, which she calls unlawful.
Size and accountability of government
Proposes a state Department of Government Efficiency to cut waste and bureaucracy, plus complete audits of state departments.
Education
Supports local control, parental involvement, individualized learning, pay tied to teacher results, and limits on student cell phone use during class.
Economy and cost of living
Proposes ending state corporate incentive deals, saying recent packages delivered few of the jobs promised. Supports cutting red tape so small manufacturers, farms, trades and family businesses can grow.
Energy / utilities
Says Michigan pays too much for electricity. Pledges to stop policies she says raise utility bills and to keep energy affordable through innovation.
Environment / Line 5
Says the DNR and EGLE have not protected natural resources. Proposes a complete audit of both agencies and an end to what she calls backroom deals that harm Michigan's ecology.
Immigration / civil rights
Supports lawful immigration and opposes immigrants depending on taxpayer-funded welfare. Proposes an audit of the immigration process and action against illegal-labor exploitation and human trafficking.

Background

  • U.S. Taxpayers Party nominee for Michigan governor, 2026 (nominated at the party convention in July 2026)
  • Chair, U.S. Taxpayers Party of Michigan
  • U.S. Taxpayers Party nominee for governor, 2022 (about 0.4% of the vote, 16,246 votes)
  • Disqualified from the 2022 Republican primary ballot over fraudulent petition signatures
  • Business owner in real estate, farming, technology and energy
  • Founder of Bereavement Research; horse rescue work
  • Education: bachelor's degree
